messages:
Maya: Anyone see a weird latency pattern in ap-south1 this morning? P90 for hosted-chat bumped ~2.5x at 07:12. Noticed a cluster-level egress blip and GPU busy counters climbed.
Rohit: yes. I traced to a set of nightly model exports from team 'research-lab' (annotation export-heavy=true). They were pushing parallel shards to object storage.
Maya: are they on shared nodes or a reserved slice?
Rohit: shared. They requested cost-savings so we colocated. Bad idea in hindsight.
ops-bot: alert: ap-south1 cluster: p90_latency_up (07:12). Related metric: egress_tx_top_nodes. Incident ID: INC-4999.
Leo: can we throttle their egress path at the node level? We have a programmable policer in the fabric but it's per-pod only if pods carry label infra/egress-tier.
Kim: they don't. But we can temporarily taint the nodes or cordon a few to redirect their jobs to quieter hosts. That risks OOM churn.
Victor: simpler: set a per-namespace egress cap via CNI policer for research-lab namespace to 1.5Gbps burst. Quick, reversible.
Maya: do it. Apply and monitor. Also push a KV-cache freeze for serving pods for 10 min to prevent rebuild storms.
Rohit: starting the CNI change now. will annotate namespace `infra.egress=research-throttle`.
Leo: note: fabric ACLs will log a config-change. pinging @netops for oversight.
ops-bot: config-note: Egress policer applied to ns/research-lab by Rohit at 07:22. Change ID: CFG-7878.
Kim: monitoring UI: egress drops from top nodes down from ~8Gbps to ~2Gbps, serving p90 trending down.
Victor: one caveat: the research jobs still hold GPU memory and cause local NVLink traffic; throttling egress reduces S3 spikes but not intra-node memory pressure. We might need to reschedule.
Maya: good call. Can we preemptively migrate the checkpointing pods to a dedicated ephemeral pool (label pool=ephemeral-checkpoints) while they run the rest of the night?
Rohit: I can trigger a migration via alloc-controller if we create the pool. provisioning estimate: 4x A100 small slices for 8h. Cost: rough ballpark $1.1k.
Leo: add to PR for approval; we can fund from cloud-ops burst budget.
Maya: also add a job-template change: default checkpoint concurrency=1 and randomized upload jitter. That should prevent synchronized spikes.
Victor: agree. For medium-term, let's add a scheduler anti-affinity rule: `no_cohost_with: serving-sensitive=true` for any job with `export-heavy=true`.
Kim: I'll draft the RFC. Also will add a metric to detect synchronous multi-pod uploads (upload_fanout > 3) and alert earlier.
Maya: owners: Rohit -> apply namespace policer + migration plan; Kim -> RFC + alert; Victor -> job-template change PR; Leo -> cost approval. Check back in 45m.
Rohit: migration staged, starting node drain for pods flagged export-heavy. Will roll gracefully.
ops-bot: note: automated drain will respect preemption_policy=graceful; estimated window 6m per node.
Maya: thanks. If this recurs we should force a hard partition: dedicated checkpoint pool only. For now the throttles look good.
Kim: logging INFRA-exports-2026 in backlog.
Victor: testing idea in staging tonight: simulate 10 parallel shard uploads across 6 nodes to validate policer + migration. Will report results.
Maya: perfect. :thumbsup:
